title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 23
statement: Three balls are randomly and independently tossed into bins numbered with the positive integers so that for each ball, the probability that it is tossed into bin \(i\) is \(2^{-i}\) for \(i=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots.\) More than one ball is allowed in each bin. The probability that the balls end up evenly spaced in distinct bins is \(\dfrac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. (For example, the balls are evenly spaced if they are tossed into bins \(3,\) \(17,\) and \(10.\)) What is \(p+q?\)

solutions.text:
Evenly spaced distinct bins form an arithmetic progression \(n,n+d,n+2d\) with \(n,d\ge 1.\) The three labels sum to \(3(n+d),\) so a fixed assignment of balls to these bins has probability \(2^{-3(n+d)}.\)

The three balls can be ordered in \(3!=6\) ways, so the total probability is \(6\sum_{n\ge 1}\sum_{d\ge 1}2^{-3(n+d)}\) \(=6\left(\sum_{n\ge 1}\tfrac{1}{8^n}\right)^2\) \(=6\cdot\tfrac17\cdot\tfrac17=\tfrac{6}{49}.\)

Since \(\gcd(6,49)=1,\) we get \(p+q=6+49=55.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Evenly spaced means the bins are \(n, n+d, n+2d\) for some \(n,d\ge 1;\) their labels sum to \(3(n+d)\)
Each such ordered assignment has probability \(2^{-3(n+d)},\) and there are \(3!\) orderings of the three balls
